fixes.explanation: That's what Luke 6:1 says: the disciples "…began to pick the heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat them." No oven, no timer, no cooling rack. Just hands and a walk through a field. I've baked a lot of batches, and even I have never made a snack that fast.

Baskets and selling never show up in this verse. Luke 6:1 says the disciples rub the grain in their hands and eat it. Nobody is running a grain stand here. I think the only business going on is eating.

True, and it's right there in Luke 6:4: David "…entered the house of God…" He did this when he and his companions were hungry. Jesus brings up that moment after some of the Pharisees ask their question about the Sabbath. I'd say Jesus really did bring the receipts.

This one's actually true. Luke 6:4 says David "…entered the house of God…" He did this when he and his companions were hungry. Jesus brings it up after some of the Pharisees ask their question about the Sabbath. No stress, baker, now you've got it for next time.

Interesting guess, but that's not what the verse says. Luke 6:4 says the bread is "…lawful only for the priests to eat." That's why Jesus' example stands out. David ate what was set apart for the priests.

Right. Luke 6:8 says Jesus told the man, "Get up and stand among us." And the man "…got up and stood there." Jesus does this knowing their thoughts, while the scribes and Pharisees are watching Him closely. I think the man needed some courage right then.
That's not what Jesus says. In Luke 6:8 He tells the man, "Get up and stand among us." The man gets up and stands there, among them. Nothing about outside.
Jesus doesn't send him away. Luke 6:8 says He told the man, "Get up and stand among us." and the man "…got up and stood there." Right then, among them. No other day needed.
True. Luke 6:11 says the scribes and Pharisees "…began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus." They talk it over together. The story isn't over.
This one is true, baker. Luke 6:11 says the scribes and Pharisees "…began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus." They talk it over together. The story isn't over.
